text.L1: Fractions are numbers, so they have places on a number line.
text.L2: The bottom number tells how many equal gaps to make from 0 to 1.
text.L3: Count gaps, not marks. Four marks between 0 and 1 make five equal gaps.
text.L4: So each gap is one fifth. The top number tells how many gaps to count from 0.
text.L5: To mark two fifths, count two gaps from 0. That mark is 2/5.
text.L6: A fraction can also go beyond 1. If the top number is bigger than the bottom number, it lies past 1.
text.L7: For example, 5/4 is one quarter past 1, so it is after 1.
text.L8: Now use these ideas to choose where 5/4 belongs.
